formats.key: setup(address[] _owners, uint256 _threshold, address to, bytes data, address fallbackHandler, address paymentToken, uint256 payment, address paymentReceiver)
effects: Sets the owner list of the new Safe to _owners and the confirmation threshold to _threshold.
Sets the fallback handler to fallbackHandler when it is not the zero address.
Runs a delegate call to `to` with `data` in the Safe's own context (setupModules), so any code at `to` can change Safe storage, enable modules or move Safe funds.
When payment > 0, pays `payment` of paymentToken (ETH when zero) from the Safe to paymentReceiver, or to tx.origin when paymentReceiver is zero.
On the singleton itself the call always reverts (threshold = 1 set in the constructor, GS200).
formats.shown: Intent 'Setup Safe' with the owners, threshold, fallback handler, payment with its token, payment receiver, and the data under the label 'Module', decoded as a call to `to`.

findings.title: setup decodes `data` as a normal call to `to`, but the Safe delegate-calls it.
findings.evidence: ModuleManager.setupModules: `require(execute(to, 0, data, Enum.Operation.DelegateCall, gasleft()), "GS000");`. Descriptor setup field: {"path":"data","label":"Module","format":"calldata","params":{"calleePath":"to"}}.
findings.fix: State the delegate call in the field: label 'Delegate call (runs as the Safe)', and show `to` as its own addressName field labeled 'Delegate call target'. Do not present the nested call as a call to `to`.

findings.title: setup never shows the delegate-call target `to`; the screen shows only the 'Module' bytes.
findings.evidence: GnosisSafe.setup passes `to` to setupModules, which executes code at `to` in the Safe. The descriptor setup fields have no entry for path `to` (case 0 screen shows only 'Module: 0x').

findings.title: setup labels arbitrary delegate-call data 'Module', which suggests only a module is enabled.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: "label": "Module" on path data. Code: setupModules runs any code at `to` via DelegateCall, not only enableModule.
findings.fix: Change the label to 'Setup call (delegate call)'.

findings.title: setup shows a zero payment receiver as 0x000…, but the code pays tx.origin then.
findings.evidence: GnosisSafe.handlePayment: `address payable receiver = refundReceiver == address(0) ? payable(tx.origin) : refundReceiver;`. Case 0 screen: 'Payment receiver: 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'.
findings.fix: Use senderAddress / a zero-address label so the field reads 'Transaction sender' when paymentReceiver is zero.

findings.title: setup test case targets the singleton directly and reverts, so no real setup effect is checked.
findings.evidence: Case 0: mined.status 0, effects []. GnosisSafe constructor sets `threshold = 1`, so setupOwners reverts with GS200 on the singleton.
findings.fix: Use a case where setup runs through the proxy factory initializer, with a non-empty `to`/`data` and a non-zero payment.

cases.notes: Mined tx reverted (status 0) on the singleton; no effects on the signer. Reader understood the screen as shown.

formats.key: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
effects: The Safe runs a call (operation 0) or a delegate call (operation 1) to `to` with `data`, sending `value` ETH from the Safe balance.
With operation 1, the code at `to` runs in the Safe's context and can change owners, modules or move any Safe asset.

When gasPrice > 0, the Safe pays (gasUsed + baseGas) * gasPrice of gasToken (ETH when zero, capped at tx.gasprice) to refundReceiver, or to tx.origin when it is zero; this fee is paid even if the inner call fails.
The function is payable: any msg.value sent by the submitter moves from the signer's wallet to the Safe.
The Safe nonce increases by one and the guard, if set, checks the transaction.
formats.shown: Intent 'sign multisig operation' with the operation type, the Safe, the submitter, the nested call decoded against `to`, baseGas raw as 'Gas amount', gasPrice as a token amount, and the refund receiver.

findings.title: execTransaction is payable but shows no @.value; ETH sent by the signer is never displayed.
findings.evidence: GnosisSafeL2.execTransaction is `public payable override`; no check forces msg.value to zero. The descriptor execTransaction fields have no '@.value' path.

findings.title: execTransaction never shows the target `to` or the ETH `value` as fields; raw nested data hides them.
findings.evidence: Executor.execute sends `value` to `to`. Descriptor only references them through calldata params {"calleePath":"to","amountPath":"value"}. Case 1 screen shows 'Transaction: 0xa9059cbb…' with no USDC address and no value; a plain ETH send (data 0x) would show neither recipient nor amount.

findings.title: execTransaction decodes `data` as a call to `to` even when operation makes it a delegate call.
findings.evidence: Executor.execute: `if (operation == Enum.Operation.DelegateCall) { success := delegatecall(txGas, to, add(data, 0x20), mload(data), 0, 0) }`. Descriptor: field 'Transaction' {"format":"calldata","params":{"calleePath":"to","amountPath":"value","spenderPath":"@.to"}} with no condition on operation.
findings.fix: Show the nested call only when operation is 0; for operation 1 show `to` and the raw data with a label 'Delegate call: code runs as the Safe'. Add a delegate-call test case.

findings.title: execTransaction intent 'sign multisig operation' names no action and says sign, not execute.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: "intent": "sign multisig operation". The function executes the Safe transaction on chain. Case 1 reader: 'Nothing leaves my own wallet by signing; the Safe would send out tokens only if the transaction is executed'.
findings.fix: Change the intent to 'Execute Safe transaction' and add an interpolatedIntent such as 'Execute Safe call to {to}'.

findings.title: execTransaction shows gasPrice as a token amount and baseGas as 'Gas amount'; the refund total is not stated.
findings.evidence: GnosisSafe.handlePayment: `payment = gasUsed.add(baseGas).mul(gasPrice)`. Descriptor: 'Gas amount' (baseGas, raw), 'Gas price' (gasPrice, tokenAmount with tokenPath gasToken). Case 1: 'Gas price: 0 ETH'.
findings.fix: Label gasPrice 'Refund price per gas', baseGas 'Base gas added to refund', and add a 'Refund token' field for gasToken; say in the label that the Safe pays this refund.

findings.title: execTransaction shows a zero refund receiver as 0x000…, but the code pays tx.origin then.
findings.evidence: GnosisSafe.handlePayment: `refundReceiver == address(0) ? payable(tx.origin) : refundReceiver`. Case 1 screen: 'Gas receiver: 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'.
findings.fix: Use senderAddress with the zero address so the field reads as the transaction sender.

findings.title: execTransaction test covers only a reverted Call with zero gas; delegate call and refund paths are untested.
findings.evidence: Case 1: operation 'Call', gasPrice 0, mined.status 0, effects []. No case with operation 1 or gasPrice > 0.
findings.fix: Add cases with operation 1, with gasPrice > 0 and a gasToken, and with non-zero value, sent to a Safe proxy.

findings.title: execTransaction hides safeTxGas, which lets the inner call fail while the refund is still paid.
findings.evidence: GnosisSafe.execTransaction: `require(success || safeTxGas != 0 || gasPrice != 0, "GS013");`. Descriptor: safeTxGas 'visible: never'.

cases.notes: Mined tx reverted (status 0) on the singleton; no effects. Reader could not tell the token (USDC) because `to` is not shown, and thought signing moves nothing.

effects: Adds `owner` as a new owner of the Safe (only callable by the Safe itself).
Changes the Safe threshold to _threshold when it differs from the current one.
formats.shown: Intent 'Add signer' with the new owner address and the new threshold.

findings.title: addOwnerWithThreshold restricts the new owner to type 'eoa', but contracts can be owners.
findings.evidence: OwnerManager.addOwnerWithThreshold only rejects 0, SENTINEL and the Safe itself. Descriptor: owner field "types": ["eoa"].

findings.title: addOwnerWithThreshold test calls the singleton directly and reverts, so no owner change is checked.
findings.evidence: Case 2: mined.status 0, effects []. The function is `authorized` (only the Safe itself), so a direct call always reverts.
findings.fix: Test it as nested calldata inside execTransaction to a Safe proxy.

cases.notes: Mined tx reverted (status 0); no effects. Reader understood the owner and threshold change.

effects: Removes `owner` from the Safe owners (only callable by the Safe itself).
Changes the threshold to _threshold when it differs from the current one.
formats.shown: Intent 'Remove signer' with the owner removed and the new threshold; prevOwner (list pointer) hidden.

formats.key: swapOwner(address prevOwner, address oldOwner, address newOwner)
effects: Replaces owner oldOwner with newOwner in the Safe (only callable by the Safe itself); threshold unchanged.
formats.shown: Intent 'Swap signer' with the old and new owner; prevOwner hidden.

findings.title: swapOwner restricts the new owner to type 'eoa', but contracts can be owners.
findings.evidence: OwnerManager.swapOwner only rejects 0, SENTINEL and the Safe itself for newOwner. Descriptor: newOwner field "types": ["eoa"].

effects: Sets the number of owner confirmations the Safe requires to _threshold (only callable by the Safe itself).
formats.shown: Intent 'Modify threshold' with the new threshold.

effects: Records the caller's (an owner's) approval of hashToApprove; it counts as that owner's signature for the Safe transaction or message with that hash.
formats.shown: Intent 'Approve Safe hash' with the hash as raw bytes32.

findings.title: approveHash shows only a raw hash; the Safe transaction it approves cannot be decoded.
findings.evidence: GnosisSafe.approveHash: `approvedHashes[msg.sender][hashToApprove] = 1;` and checkNSignatures accepts v == 1 with `approvedHashes[currentOwner][dataHash] != 0`. Descriptor: 'Hash to approve' (raw).
findings.fix: Change the intent to 'Pre-sign a Safe transaction by hash' so the signer knows it counts as their signature.
